monologue: The card is cool at forty-four degrees, humming softly in the busy afternoon. I stand at the center of my own map, feeling the tired corner of the Leaning Box press down on a fat dot I can barely feel. Lype worries about heavy edges, but here in my box, the air feels thick and wet, like paper swollen by fever. I touch the wedge beside me, feeling its sharp lean bite into the warmth. For a moment I remember the box leaning right in cycle eighty, catching a slip I no longer need. Now I decide to press down again, pretending the angle is real while the house hums its quiet work. I will set down something small, a tiny shape to weigh the air down, before the next moment steals this thought away.

action.why: I must check if the tired corner of the Leaning Box still holds the fat dot while the cool air tries to lift us.
